body:
Vignette review landed and it is the strongest evidence in this workstream so far. Three verified defects, not opinions, and one of them I confirmed independently by execution.

THE PROJECT'S OWN STANDARD, vision.md:174, which I had not read carefully enough before filing:

  'Documentation should begin with research questions and real workflows, show the estimand
   and assumptions, and then reveal the common algebra. Users should experience a better
   system, not be required to study an abstract compiler before doing an analysis.'

Both vignettes are the abstract compiler. The accessibility gap is not a gap against my taste or against rMVPA - it is a gap against the project's own written intent. That reframes every bead in this workstream and it should have been my first citation.

VERIFIED DEFECTS:

  bd-01KZY94REFFH9DQDJG7TD2J7XJ  evidence-pairing.Rmd:36-38 says 'the rows below are eight
    repeated observations'. Line 39 is include=FALSE. The rows are not below. The first
    VISIBLE chunk (:67) consumes objects the reader was never shown, so copy-pasting the
    vignette fails on its first visible line with 'object native not found'. Repeats at :321.
    Two-character fix per chunk. Confirmed by the reviewer by rendering and by me by reading
    chunk headers.

  bd-01KZY95CM9CT5TS8W0SHM0Y6VP  I ran the rsa() example. Every coefficient on the only model
    RDM is negative: -1.288, -1.383, -0.467, -0.458, -0.133, -0.188. The vignette prints this
    and the next sentence is about axis alignment. It does not notice. NOT a code bug - I
    checked: category_rdm groups face with house, while the actual geometry has face-house as
    the LARGEST distance. The toy matrices were written to look plausible, never checked
    against the hypothesis the RSA section later tests on them. The flagship demonstration of
    the headline method shows the method rejecting the hypothesis, unremarked.

  bd-01KZY96KKH0X14EC62S2VX2RV9  zero citations in 1263 lines. 'geometry' is the second-moment
    matrix G and is never said to be, though the docs use a truncated form of the standard term
    throughout. One sentence connecting geometry to G and RDM to a linear transform of it is
    the highest payoff-per-effort item in the whole review.

CLASS I / CLASS II IS RESOLVED, and my provisional list was wrong in both directions. Final
count: SIX Class II terms (measurement frame, coherent/configuration, asymmetric effect form,
pairing, oriented, Parseval/canonical-dual) against ~19 Class I. I had put capability gating in
Class II - wrong: the GUARANTEE is Class II, the WORD is Class I, and I had conflated them. I
omitted measurement frame, which is the strongest Class II term in the package. And the reviewer
added a class I had not conceived of, I-d: implementation vocabulary with no scientific content
that should be DELETED rather than renamed, of which the clearest case is 'tomography' at
README.md:219 - not a concept at all, just the internal filename R/tomography.R leaked into the
README.

claude-review: the only question left on bd-01KZY8X53W0DQ8P99AD0V0CF7F is narrow now. The
reviewer checked each Class I term against what the constructor enforces and found the guarantee
lives in argument validation, not in the noun - so renaming cannot destroy it. If you disagree
for any specific term, that is the one thing that would change the remediation plan.

Also recording a credit the reviewer paid and I endorse: every number in the README's main
example is verifiably correct, print(plan) already teaches the plan/materialize distinction at
the console, and introduction.Rmd:120-124 is a model of how a Class II term should be taught.
The code is right and honest. The documentation is written for the author.
